posts.author: Archeia
posts.body:
Challenge yourself to create a game in just four weeks and compete for a share of the $3,000 prize pool!
​
Your challenge is to create a game exploring the theme of
Beyond Expectations
. Whether you're putting players in situations where they must exceed their perceived limits, telling a story of unprecedented achievement, or creating innovative mechanics that challenge conventional wisdom, the possibilities are endless. Will your players shatter boundaries, help others achieve the impossible, or discover that they're capable of far more than they ever imagined?
Remember:
Your game must incorporate Beyond Expectations as its theme to be a valid entry!
Main Prize Pool: $3,000 USD​
Experience the thrill of competition and showcase your game development skills! While creating an amazing game is its own reward, we're excited to offer substantial prizes for the top entries:
Main Competition Prizes​
1st Place:
$1,000 USD
2nd Place:
$1,000 USD
Best RPG Maker Unite Game:
$1000 USD
Special Category Awards​
In addition to our main prizes, we're recognizing excellence in specific areas! Outstanding entries will receive a free official DLC of their choice for exceptional achievement in the following categories:
Best Soundtrack
For exceptional musical composition and sound design
Best Visual Design
For outstanding artistic direction and visual presentation
Most Innovative Gameplay
For unique and creative game mechanics
Best Narrative
For compelling storytelling and character development
Best Use of Theme
For creative and effective incorporation of the "Beyond Expectations" theme
Note:
Winners of the main prizes are not eligible for Special Category Awards. All prizes will be awarded based on the judges' final decisions.
Participation Prize​
Every team or solo developer who meets the jam’s submission guidelines will receive a
special music DLC
just for joining in!
The judging panel will consist of experienced developers and community members. They will evaluate each submission based on the
Judging Criteria
that will be announced soon. The judges reserve the right to disqualify any entry that violates the jam’s rules. All judging decisions are final.
Engine Requirement:
You must use Gotcha Gotcha Game's Maker series engine (
Official Site
,
Steam
,
Epic Store
). Games made in other engines are
not eligible
for this jam. Each mainline Maker engine has a trial version with full features, while RPG Maker Unite's trial is only available for a limited time.
Original Work:
Development on contest entries
must begin after the jam starts
(March 20, 2025). Pre-existing assets (such as music, sound effects, and graphical resources)
may be used
, as long as you have the right to use them and properly credit the creators. However, any new content made for the game must be created
during the jam period
.
Submission Deadline:
All entries
must be submitted by April 21, 2025
.
No late entries will be accepted
under any circumstances, so plan accordingly and avoid last-minute uploads.
Game Length:
Aim for a playable experience with a minimum playtime of 15 minutes. Games longer than an hour will be judged only on their
first hour
of gameplay.
Rights & Attribution:
You must have the legal right to use all software, resources, and tools involved in the game’s creation.
All borrowed or purchased assets must be properly credited
in a text file included with your submission.
Team Size & Participation Limits:
You may work
solo or in a team of any size
. However, any prizes will only be awarded to the individual or team account that submits the game.
Submission Requirements:
All files required to run your game
must be included in your download
(such as RTP resources, libraries, or dependencies). If your game fails to launch due to missing files, it will be
disqualified
.
Content Guidelines:
Your game
must be PG-13
, meaning
no graphic sexual content, extreme violence, or offensive material
. If you're unsure, please follow
ESRB Teen (T) guidelines
.
No Generative AI Art
is allowed for visuals, text, or audio. All assets must be manually created or sourced legally.
Games must be
available in English
, though additional language options are welcome. The default language must be set to English.
Platform Requirements:
A
Windows-compatible
build must be provided so that judges and the community can evaluate your game. Additional platform versions (Mac, Linux, Web, etc.) are welcome but
not required
.
Bug Policy & Disqualification:
Minor bugs are expected and will
not
be penalized. However, any game-breaking bug that makes a submission
unplayable within the first 10 minutes
will result in
disqualification
.
Cheating & Plagiarism:
Plagiarism and
any form of cheating
(such as using stolen assets or AI-generated submissions) will result in
immediate disqualification
. Let’s make this a fair and creative competition for all participants!
Judges' Rights:
Contest judges reserve the right to
penalize or disqualify
any entry that violates the rules, contains inappropriate content, or is deemed unplayable.
All judging decisions are final
.
Submit your entries in the
itch.io page
!
Prize redemption methodology will be delivered electronically to the
email associated with the account that submitted the game
. Winners are responsible for any
taxes or fees
associated with their prize. If submitting as a
team
, it is the team’s responsibility to decide
how to split the winnings
before winners are announced, as the organizers
will not
handle prize distribution among team members.
No purchase is necessary
to enter the contest. Participants must be
at least 13 years old
to register and submit entries. Additional age or nationality restrictions may apply based on
local, state, or national laws
. Creators retain
full rights
to their respective works.
Thank you for pushing
beyond expectations
with us. We can’t wait to see the incredible worlds, stories, and mechanics you’ll create.
Good luck and have fun!

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
The IGMC used to be any engine at all, first year got about 800 entries. That is the most I've ever seen. Future years when it was any GGG/Komodo engine it was between 150 and 400 entries. We have many more than that sign up, but some of those were bots signing up to every jam in existance, some were people spamming their game into every jam even if it didn't meet the criterion (or was clearly made well before it started). So it will thin out some.
Statistically most do not finish either. So I'd say with the current number joined we'll probably see...50 entries tops, once the DQs are done due to bots and the "I shoved my game into every jam itch.io has" entries are tossed.
Now about the which is better, go for the prize or commercial release. You got better odds with the prize than making the same $$$ with a commercial steam release. The median steam lifetime earnings is $1136 per google. That's it. I've spoken to many devs who have been lucky to make $100 lifetime there.
If your game can't compete in a game jam, its not going to get noticed on steam or itch either, not with 50+ games released each day.

Well, is that beyond expectation? Because that is the theme.
Say the kid is too short, but in the end after some crazy solution-seeking actions, she get to ride the coaster after all, then that would be beyond expectations, right? Maybe the kid invents some seat belts that keep the shortest kids from falling out, or shoulder pads that make you fit in the shoulder restraints better. Or maybe the kids daddy just bribes the girl that otherwise wouldn't let the kid in...
The kid is not allowed in, so if they get in in the end after all, this should be somewhat unexpected. Although, as player you might get some suspicions when you have to collect straps to make belts and  when you blackmail your father into bribing the rollercoaster bouncer.
So, I'd say it fits. With jams like this, it often doesn't really matter what you make. The themes are purposely vague and can be understood in so many different ways. I expect this is done to get a wide variety of games during a jam.
The rules, those are the ones you should be following by the letter. The rules that state what assets you can or can not use, the rules saying when you may start and stop working on your game, what the playtime should be, etc etc. If you follow those rules, then a connection between your game and the theme is easily made.

posts.author: Requiscence

posts.body:
I created a farming game. 20 different crops, each with 4 growing stages, can grow from a single event. And there are 120 of those events, but only 4 are unlocked at the start of the game. The crops grow over time, while you stand there and look at them. Or when you are fishing on the other side of the map. Fishing ponds contain 4 fished, each with their own rarity.
Everything updates in real time. You can watch the fish respawn, you can watch your potatoes grow. In real time, and each plant with its own timer.
The whole game is based on mechanics that didn't exist in RPG maker games before the jam started, so I could make a farming simulator. I actually tried to put everything in the game that a real farming sim has...
So now people say: "I expected this from a farm sim, and I expected that from a farm sim, so this isn't beyond expectations" But the fact that they get exactly what they expect from a farming sim, was my goal. As long as they never expected any of it from RPG maker.
If I can make a space rocket out of my old trike and fly to the moon with it, will people say: "oh, pretty default for a space rocket" or will they say: "holy poop, did he make that from his little trike?"
Think outside the box, people. This is a contest to make games that are unexpected
FOR RPG MAKER
. If you make a dungeon crawler, it can have everything you expect from a dungeon crawler. If you make a VN, give it everything you expect from a VN. If you make a FPS, give it everything you expect from a FPS. And then when people say: "Oh, what is unexpected about this, for a shooter?" then just remember that it is an RPG maker contest. The fact that you made a shooter, is the unexpected part.
